realInventory.browser-use: Research and operate rendered web pages through OpenCorvus Browser tools, including authenticated workflows and visual inspection.
realInventory.computer-use: Operate native desktop apps through OpenCorvus Computer tools when the task requires their visible interface.
realInventory.design-taste-frontend: Apply context-aware visual judgment to frontend product design and redesign work. Infer the design language from the accepted brief and evidence, use mature design systems, avoid generic generated-interface patterns, and finish through real rendered-page inspection.
realInventory.grill-me: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.
realInventory.research-report: Produce a multi-source research report — comparison matrix, capability survey, market analysis, recommendation document — backed by `websearch` (and `webfetch` only after `websearch` returns a concrete URL). Activate when the deliverable is a markdown report rather than running software, and the work is fundamentally synthesising prose from external sources rather than writing code. Signals — the brief asks for 报告 / 调研 / 对比 / 分析 / 综述 / 功能矩阵 / 评估 / 建议 / report / comparison / matrix / analysis / survey / recommendation; or compares named third-party products / platforms / vendors; or asks for a structured insight + recommendation document. Do NOT activate for code tasks, even when the code happens to consume third-party APIs.
realInventory.work-artifacts: Produce editable PPTX presentations, DOCX documents and XLSX spreadsheets through the single OpenCorvus Work Artifact Harness. Use the exact mounted typed profile. DOCX supports ordered title, heading and body paragraphs; XLSX supports bounded worksheets and literal cells. Fresh PNG review and derived PDF previews accompany DOCX/XLSX delivery. Does not edit existing files or author formulas, macros, PDF source, OCR, archives or media.
